title: P02 follow-up: lower the Muon peak LR 0.01 -> 0.008 at fixed per-step decoupled decay on the six-block 101-claude Lean incumbent
description: P02 (Muon) follow-up: MUON_LR 0.01 -> 0.008, the only edit to 101-claude's pretrain.py; MUON_WD = 10*WD*LR/MUON_LR rises to 0.125, so the per-step Muon shrinkage (lr*MUON_WD) stays exactly as before and only the orthogonalized step shrinks by 20%. 0.01 was tuned on shallower token-format models, 095-claude showed the upward move (0.012) cost -58, and the Lean-era depth gain (5 -> 6 blocks) means each Muon step now composes through one more block, so a smaller step should give a lower-noise, smaller-norm six-block starting point that expert iteration can adapt.
hypothesis: Muon's update has fixed element RMS per matrix, so the function change per step grows with the number of blocks it composes through; the peak LR was set on 4-5 block models, and 095 (0.01 -> 0.012, -58) suggests 0.01 already sits at or above the optimum. At six blocks a 20% smaller step lowers late-training update noise (val loss plateaus by mid-run, so fit is not step-limited) and, with the per-step decay unchanged, shrinks the Muon/decay equilibrium weight norm by roughly 10%, the same direction as the 3x and 10x decoupled-decay keeps (069/070). A lower-noise, smaller-norm model should be a better expert-iteration start: fewer sampled parse/unbound-name failures and more plasticity under the frozen RL AdamW, so more RL targets solved per round and more dev >= 7 solves.
expected_delta: -35 to +40 dev solves >= 7 (central +5); pretraining steps unchanged at ~3,570-3,630 (same step cost), final val loss 0.079-0.086 (may be slightly higher early, within noise at the end), totals ~1,850-2,000 s, no timeout

arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=6 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.5
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (6 per sample), unchanged fork code

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale, Polar Express orthogonalization) on hidden matrices and head.weight at peak LR 0.008; continuous AdamW auxiliary unchanged

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: CHANGED: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.008 * adam_lr / 0.001 (101-claude: 0.01)
muon.parameters: All 24 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 6 blocks) plus head.weight (107,256; vocab 107, no bias) are in Muon: 25 matrices. Six qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (107<256) so it is not transposed.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.
muon.lr_change: CHANGED vs 101-claude: MUON_LR 0.01 -> 0.008 (-20%). MUON_WD is derived as 10*WD*LR/MUON_LR = 0.125 (was 0.1), so per-step Muon shrinkage lr_eff*MUON_WD = 10*WD*adam_lr (peak 1e-3) is unchanged; only the update step is 20% smaller.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged per-step rule from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR, now 0.125 at MUON_LR 0.008, so Muon per-step shrinkage (peak 1e-3 per step) is still ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Same as 101-claude: fork default construction, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Same RNG stream as 101-claude.
